title: Guard deprecated concat copy keyword by pandas version in src/utils/file_io.py
body:
Fixes #894

## Changes

Guard the deprecated `copy` keyword of `pd.concat` by pandas version in
`src/utils/file_io.py`, so behaviour is preserved on every supported
version:

- `src/utils/file_io.py`: module-level
  `PANDAS_VERSION = Version(pd.__version__)` (from `packaging`, already a
  transitive dependency of pandas), and at both call sites:

  ```python
  if PANDAS_VERSION < Version("3.0"):
      final_df = pd.concat(dfs, keys=coll_levels, axis=1, join="inner", copy=False)
  else:
      final_df = pd.concat(dfs, keys=coll_levels, axis=1, join="inner")
  ```

  and

  ```python
  if PANDAS_VERSION < Version("3.0"):
      all = pd.concat([all, tmp_df[SE_idx]], axis=1, copy=False)
  else:
      all = pd.concat([all, tmp_df[SE_idx]], axis=1)
  ```

  — the same pattern as NVIDIA/cuml#8142.

## Verification

The `copy` keyword never affects the **result** of `concat` on any
pandas version, only whether input buffers are copied; the branch keeps
that behaviour exactly as it was on each side of the boundary. Runtime
checks in isolated venvs:

- pandas 2.3.3 takes the `copy=False` branch: identical results to
  today's code (`keys` MultiIndex with `join="inner"`; `SE_idx` column
  append), no warning.
- pandas 3.0.5 takes the plain branch: no `Pandas4Warning` is emitted,
  results identical (the `copy` keyword is a documented no-op under
  Copy-on-Write).
- Modified file passes `python -m py_compile`.

title: Bottleneck Characterization
body:
This PR builds off of #242 which added "Bottleneck Characterization" to Omniperf, consisting of

- End-to-end Runtime Classification plot
- GPU Kernel Runtime Breakdown plot

I have modified the code so that the characterization and plotting modules match Omniperf's class based structure. See original PR for the feature's methodology and docs

### Usage
To use the "Bottleneck Characterization" feature, just ensure omnitrace (specifically `omnitrace-instrument`) is available on your PATH. Omniperf will automatically run instrumentation as part of its profiling pipeline (disable using `--no-trace`). You can find your .proto output file in the standard Omniperf output directory.

Use analyze mode to generate the output plots (.pdf versions will also be saved by default). If for whatever reason you'd like to explicitly specify a .proto trace file you can do so in analysis using the `--trace` flag.

```console
omniperf analyze -p workloads/dummy/MI200 --trace dummy_app.proto --gui
```

You'll notice the standalone GUI view now highlights these two plots in the previously empty top section of the webpage
![image](https://github.com/ROCm/omniperf/assets/11466906/1fb4044e-ffb5-4f09-b14c-20986b2d65c7)


### Todo

- [x] Enable `--bottleneck-trace` option to be used without `--gui`

title: Move roofline plot generation to analyze mode
body:
This is to address https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/issues/435

> Still, the only thing I need would be a way to generate the roofline PDFs for a given kernel after having recorded performance counters for all kernel.
> 
> I believe that would be a useful feature because we don't want to re-profile the whole program each time we want a roofline for a different kernel. This feature seems to already exist in the GUI, I would appreciate having the same capabilities built in the CLI

By moving the creation of the roofline plot pdfs to analyze mode on cli, we can create a roofline plots with different kernel filtering without having to re-profile the whole program.

This fixes https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/issues/777 and https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/issues/786 for me.

My guess for the `1704` -> `1705` change is that a new section was added but the following section numbers were not correctly updated in `gui.py`

I hope that the rest of the ids in https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/blob/61a9381edfd781cdbef83aa8837d77531bbb661f/src/rocprof_compute_analyze/analysis_webui.py#L54-L59 are correct, especially the id `1701` for which I was hitting the `HBM Bandwidth` key error https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/issues/786. It seems `HBM Bandwidth` was introduced in https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/pull/632 (not clear why), so I am not sure whether this fix is correct - or whether 1701 should be now 1702 for example.

Also `determine_chart_type` was trying to build a table chart using an empty dataframe which yielded errors.

# Before: Output before the fix and what is wrong here

`ROCPROFCOMPUTE_LOGLEVEL=debug rocprof-compute analyze -p workloads/mykernel/MI355/ --gui` crashing when selecting a kernel, with several crashes fixed in this PR.

# After: Output after this fix and how is it fixed

rocprof-compute GUI works.

# Explanation of fix

* Table id `1704` is wrong in the code and should be `1705`.
* A section for `HBM Bandwidth` is missing in https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/blob/develop/src/rocprof_compute_soc/analysis_configs/gfx950/1700_L2_cache.yaml
* A table is empty and there is no check for empty tables yield later crashes (see https://github.com/ROCm/rocprofiler-compute/pull/787#discussion_r2222294101)
